name: Razor Rat
description:
The Razor Rat is a large, heavily built rodent averaging 60–80 cm from nose to tail, distinguished by the pronounced keratinized spine-ridges running in parallel rows along its dorsal surface from the base of the skull to the tail root. These ridges are not true spines but compressed keratin plates, similar in structure to a pangolin's scales, that have hardened over generations of contact with razor-wire fencing. The fur between the ridges is coarse and oil-slicked, resistant to most surface-contact irritants. Eyes are small and deeply recessed beneath brow-ridges, protecting them from wire snag. The tail is thick and semi-prehensile, wrapped in tough segmented skin.

Razor Rats navigate the razor-wire and barbed security fencing that divides GLMZ's lower districts with near-total impunity. Their ridge anatomy deflects wire tines rather than snagging them, and observed behavior suggests they use wire-topped walls as transit corridors specifically to avoid ground-level predators and human foot traffic. They are omnivores with a strong preference for processed grain waste, insulation foam, and any protein source available — including smaller rodents. Pack sizes run 6–20 individuals with a dominant breeding pair. Litter cycles are aggressive: up to four litters per year.

In Tier 1 districts, Razor Rats are so ubiquitous they function as a kind of ambient measurement of neighborhood decay — a building overrun with them signals failing infrastructure and absent maintenance. Pest control runners who specialize in them are called ridgers or ridge-wranglers, and a few earn real money selling the keratin plates to low-end crafters who use them as cheap armor inserts or decorative material. Street kids in some neighborhoods have developed games involving placing bets on which rat can clear a wire obstacle fastest.
diet: Omnivore — grain waste, insulation foam, carrion, smaller rodents, electrical cable sheathing
notable_traits: Keratinized dorsal spine-ridges deflect razor wire
Recessed eyes protected from snag injury
encounters: Encountered almost anywhere in Tier 1–2 districts, especially at dusk and night. They move in loose packs along wire-topped walls and chain-link fencing. Most encounters are passive — they scatter when approached — but cornered individuals or protective breeding pairs will bite aggressively. Pest control contractors encounter them regularly. Street-level food vendors lose significant stock to them.
known_uses: Keratin ridge plates sold to crafters as cheap armor inserts and decorative material (Φ 2–5 per set). Occasionally eaten in desperate Tier 1 communities — described as gamey and tough. Pest control runners charge Φ 15–40 per infestation call.
story_hooks: A crafter's new cheap armor insert stock turns out to be Razor Rat plates — it works, but sourcing it leads back to a pest runner with a very strange side operation
A Tier 1 building super claims the Razor Rats in her block have started acting coordinated in ways she can't explain — moving in synchronized patterns, blocking access to a specific sub-basement
